knowledge_point.title: Calculating Indefinite Integrals Using Substitution with Inverse Secant

question.:question/worked-solution:
Note that we can rewrite this integral as

$$
\int \frac{3}{|2x|\sqrt{(2x)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x=3\,\int \frac{1}{|2x|\sqrt{(2x)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

This integral now resembles the basic one for $\text{arcsec},$

$$
\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\text{d}u=\text{arcsec}(u)+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of $u$ as the variable, we have $2x.$

So, let's substitute $u=2x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\,\int \frac{1}{|2x|\sqrt{(2x)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x &=3\,\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{(u)^{2}-1}}\cdot (\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u) \\ &=\frac{3}{2}\,\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{(u)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}u \\ &=\frac{3}{2}\,\text{arcsec}(u)+C \\ &=\frac{3}{2}\,\text{arcsec}(2x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: Real x with |slope*x|>1; principal real arcsec. Each connected component has an independent arbitrary constant C.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Note that we can rewrite this integral as

$$
\int \frac{2}{|x|\sqrt{36x^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x=12\,\int \frac{1}{|6x|\sqrt{(6x)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

This integral now resembles the basic one for $\text{arcsec},$

$$
\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\text{d}u=\text{arcsec}(u)+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of $u$ as the variable, we have $6x.$

So, let's substitute $u=6x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{6}\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{|x|\sqrt{36x^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x &=12\,\int \frac{1}{|6x|\sqrt{(6x)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x \\ &=12\,\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{(u)^{2}-1}}\cdot (\frac{1}{6}\text{d}u) \\ &=2\,\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{(u)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}u \\ &=2\,\text{arcsec}(u)+C \\ &=2\,\text{arcsec}(6x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we can rewrite this integral as

$$
\int \frac{6}{|x|\sqrt{25x^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{30}{|5x|\sqrt{(5x)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

This integral now resembles the basic one for $\text{arcsec},$

$$
\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\text{d}u=\text{arcsec}(u)+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of $u$ as the variable, we have $5x.$

So, let's substitute $u=5x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{5}\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{6}{|x|\sqrt{25x^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x &=\int \frac{30}{|5x|\sqrt{(5x)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x \\ &=30\,\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{(u)^{2}-1}}\cdot (\frac{1}{5}\text{d}u) \\ &=30\,\cdot\frac{1}{5}\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{(u)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}u \\ &=6\,\text{arcsec}(u)+C \\ &=6\,\text{arcsec}(5x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: Real x with |slope*x|>1; principal real arcsec. Each connected component has an independent arbitrary constant C.

Note that we can rewrite this integral as

$$
\int \frac{5}{|x|\sqrt{81x^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{45}{|9x|\sqrt{(9x)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

This integral now resembles the basic one for $\text{arcsec},$

$$
\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{u^{2}-1}}\text{d}u=\text{arcsec}(u)+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of $u$ as the variable, we have $9x.$

So, let's substitute $u=9x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=9\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{9}\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5}{|x|\sqrt{81x^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x &=\int \frac{45}{|9x|\sqrt{(9x)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x \\ &=45\,\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{(u)^{2}-1}}\cdot (\frac{1}{9}\text{d}u) \\ &=45\,\cdot\frac{1}{9}\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{(u)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}u \\ &=5\,\text{arcsec}(u)+C \\ &=5\,\text{arcsec}(9x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: Real x with |slope*x|>1; principal real arcsec. Each connected component has an independent arbitrary constant C.
